content: Write 'if [ cond ]; then cmd; fi', never '[ cond ] && cmd', in any script that runs under set -e - and especially in PHP/JS-generated script strings, where the failure surfaces on a remote host during provisioning rather than in a test. Being called from an if condition suspends set -e and hides the bug, so do not treat 'it works today' as evidence. Run bash -n over the generated script in a test; it catches syntax but not this, so the rule has to be habitual.
context: The apt-source pruner emitted '[ "${base}" = "ubuntu.sources" ] && continue'. When the test is false the whole AND-list returns 1, which under set -euo pipefail exits the script - on the common path, not the edge case. It was masked only because the function happened to be called from an if condition, where set -e is suspended for the entire function body.
title: In a generated bash script under set -e, use if/fi instead of '[ test ] && command'
